newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Hongkong and Shanghai alters Sydney plans.
newsitem.headline: Hongkong and Shanghai alters Sydney plans.

text.p: The developer of a controversial apartment block project near Sydney's famous Opera House said on Thursday it has submitted a fresh development application in an effort to build a hotel on the site.
Luxury hotel group Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels Ltd (HSH) said its proposal had received a positive intitial response from government and planning authorities.

HSH director of financial and corporate services Douglas Webster acknowledged at a news conference that public protests had played a role in the new proposal and said he was surprised at their intensity.
"The protests were taken into account in the decision making process, yes," Webster said.

HSH, which operates the Peninsula hotel group, has been keen to build a hotel on the harbourside site but was unable to squeeze a hotel between two apartment blocks to the satisfaction of either itself or planners.
Webster said the new proposal scrapped one of the apartment blocks and meant the new 230-room hotel would be sited further back from the quay, and its overall bulk would be reduced.
A hotel on the site -- which will include a two-storey collonade as well as shops, cinemas and restaurants -- would also increase public access and create employment, he said.
Webster said the new proposal meant HSH's economic return would be "further down the road".
If approved, the new hotel would be completed in time for the Sydney 2000 Olympics, he added.
Work on the first apartment building on the eastern arm of the Quay prompted a flood of criticism and two demonstrations on the steps of the Opera House.
Opponents say the development is too high and too wide and will spoil views of the Opera House and neighbouring botanical gardens.

The developers counter that the site has been used for commercial buildings since 1807 and that the present proposal is much lower than the 1950s and '60s highrise buildings torn down several years ago.
